question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to register manifest-provided stdio and shared global MCP declarations directly, or must those declarations pass through a host-authorized broker/namespace before they enter `mcp.servers`?
rationale: The implementation choice determines the durable execution and cross-Claw ownership boundary; it cannot be settled safely by a mechanical patch because it changes what third-party bundle content may authorize on an operator's host.

options.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP ownership
options.body: Permit this feature only after stdio commands and shared declarations are constrained by an explicit host authorization contract with focused compatibility and lifecycle proof.

options.title: Accept direct global ownership experimentally
options.body: Merge the current model only with explicit maintainer acceptance that `--yes` authorizes globally shared executable or remote MCP declarations and their operator recovery burden.

options.title: Keep the stack paused pending the RFC
options.body: Defer this slice until the Claws RFC specifies the canonical owner and safety model for MCP resources.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP ownership
recommendation.body: Permit this feature only after stdio commands and shared declarations are constrained by an explicit host authorization contract with focused compatibility and lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned reviewer and most recent contributor to the lifecycle/removal contracts that must implement whichever ownership boundary is selected.
